assessment.nobel_worthiness: Anyonic statistics is a conceptually deep and original result: in two dimensions particles need not be bosons or fermions, and the 1977 prediction has become a cornerstone of topological quantum matter. It is a clear case of theory identifying a new possibility and nature then being shown to realise it.
assessment.attribution: Leinaas and Myrheim made the original prediction for identical particles in low dimensions. Heiblum is proposed for the experimental leg, as a pioneer of fractional-charge and interferometric detection in fractional quantum Hall systems. Fève and Manfra (and Rosenow on the theory of the interferometer) have strong claims too, so the experimental credit is not cleanly resolved by a three-person limit.
assessment.maturity: Braiding and exchange statistics were demonstrated in independent experiments around 2020 (collider and interferometer geometries) and have been reproduced and refined since. Recognition looks timely, although some interferometer interpretations have been debated.
uncertainties: Which experimental group has the decisive claim is unresolved; I rely on memory of the 2020 experiments and have not verified details.
Whether non-Abelian statistics, not yet established, would be treated as a separate later discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, and the identification of a first source such as TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane, opened neutrino astronomy. This is a discovery in nature in the sense I value, with clear lasting impact on multi-messenger astrophysics.
assessment.attribution: IceCube is a very large collaboration. Halzen is widely seen as the conceptual and organisational driver of the detector; Karle is a leading figure in construction and in the detector design and early analysis. Yoshida is credited but I judge his contribution less decisive. Any three-person configuration risks leaving out other leaders, which the committee would need to weigh.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux was established in 2013 and confirmed by multiple analyses; the source associations are more recent and still building statistics. The field is mature enough in its core result but the astrophysical origin of most neutrinos remains open.
uncertainties: Collaboration-scale attribution is difficult and the Nobel statutes limit to three.
Source identification beyond a few objects is not yet firm; I have not verified recent significance levels.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene produced a new platform for strongly correlated physics, with flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity tunable in one device. The prediction of flat bands at the magic angle followed by experiment is an exemplary theory-to-experiment story.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the flat bands at the magic angle in 2011. Jarillo-Herrero's group observed correlated insulating states and superconductivity in 2018. Other experimental groups (for example Dean, Young, Yazdani) made substantial contributions, so the configuration is defensible but incomplete.
assessment.maturity: The 2018 results were reproduced widely and the platform has generated a large literature within a few years, so impact is clear. The mechanism of superconductivity remains unsettled, which argues for some patience.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism of the superconductivity is not agreed.
Credit to the broader experimental community and to earlier theoretical work on twisted layers.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks reached fractional uncertainties at the 10^-18 level and underpin tests of fundamental physics, relativistic geodesy and a possible redefinition of the second. The invention is clean, important and with a clear measurement impact.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and realised the first strontium lattice clock; Ye drove the record accuracy and many-body, high-precision developments. The two-person configuration is natural, though Hall and Hänsch were recognised in 2005 for the related comb technology.
assessment.maturity: Many independent groups have built and compared lattice clocks; stability and accuracy have been repeatedly improved. Recognition is timely, with the redefinition of the second still pending.
uncertainties: Overlap with ion clock work and earlier frequency-comb prizes may complicate how the committee frames the discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realised the Hubbard model in a controllable setting, with the superfluid to Mott insulator transition and quantum gas microscopy giving a general platform for many-body quantum simulation. The scientific impact is broad.
assessment.attribution: Jaksch, Zoller and collaborators proposed the Bose-Hubbard realisation (Jaksch is not on the supplied list); Greiner and Bloch performed the landmark Mott insulator experiment. I propose Bloch, Cirac and Zoller as the most defensible configuration from the supplied names, noting that Greiner's claim is strong.
assessment.maturity: The core results date from about 2002 and have been widely replicated; the field is mature, though demonstrations of quantum advantage in simulation are ongoing.
uncertainties: Whether the prize would be better framed as the experimental Mott transition rather than theory proposals.
Cirac and Zoller's role overlaps with candidate B031, which affects how a prize would be allocated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Inflation explains the flatness and horizon problems and the quantum origin of cosmic structure, and its predictions of near scale-invariant adiabatic perturbations have been tested by the cosmic microwave background. Few ideas have shaped modern cosmology as much.
assessment.attribution: Guth, Linde (new inflation), and Mukhanov (quantum fluctuations as seeds) are supplied, but Starobinsky, Albrecht and Steinhardt, Sato and Chibisov are absent, so the credit configuration is genuinely contested and cannot be fairly resolved from the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Observations are consistent with inflation, but the decisive signature (primordial gravitational waves) has not been seen and the specific model is unknown. As a theorist in this area I am aware the paradigm is widely, but not universally, accepted.
uncertainties: No direct detection of the inflaton or of primordial tensor modes.
Priority disputes and omitted pioneers; I would be cautious given my own field proximity.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics provided the architecture for superconducting qubit readout and control and is central to present quantum processors. It is an enabling invention with large technological and scientific reach.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Girvin, Schoelkopf and collaborators proposed the architecture in 2004 and Wallraff with Schoelkopf demonstrated strong coupling. I propose Schoelkopf, Wallraff and Girvin as theory plus experiment, acknowledging Blais' decisive part in the proposal.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation is overwhelming and the field is mature. The 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum effects in circuits lowers urgency and creates a question of closeness to an earlier award.
uncertainties: Closeness to the recent superconducting-circuit prize.
Four credited people compete for three places.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The AdS/CFT correspondence reshaped quantum field theory and quantum gravity and gave a framework for black-hole information and strongly coupled matter. Its conceptual importance is very high.
assessment.attribution: Maldacena's 1997 conjecture is the origin; Witten and Polyakov (with Gubser and Klebanov, not supplied) gave the dictionary. Maldacena is clearly central, and the other two are plausible but less clearly decisive.
assessment.maturity: The correspondence has substantial theoretical consistency checks but no direct experimental confirmation in nature, which weighs against it for a prize that emphasises discoveries. I rank it last of my eight in part for that reason and to avoid favouring my own subfield.
uncertainties: No empirical test in our universe.
Gubser and Klebanov are not in the supplied credit, so a fair configuration is uncertain.
